target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Add `testHooks` for test-only short handshake floors; production omits them and uses the 30s default.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "codex websocket handshake timeout app-server"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A peer that accepts TCP but never completes the WS upgrade hangs `CodexAppServerClient.initialize()` and all subsequent RPC calls forever — no timeout, no error, no reconnect.
- **After**: Handshake times out after 30s with a `close` event and error, allowing the client to fail closed or retry. Working WebSocket connections are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `6c71011`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ can speak JSON-RPC over websocket transport 60ms
 ✓ can speak JSON-RPC over the canonical unix control socket 14ms
 ✓ uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay / Mattermost 3ms
 ✓ negative control: ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING on never-upgrade peer 307ms
 ✓ emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes 205ms
 ✓ fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes 206ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- Standalone production-path proof (9 structured assertions):

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

```
node=v22.22.0
head=6c710118d0c766c98543928c8fd20b21061f7d51
[case 1] negative control — ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING
  ok: without handshakeTimeout, stays CONNECTING after 300ms
  ok: readyState is CONNECTING
  info: outcome=still-pending readyState=CONNECTING wait_ms=300

[case 2] positive control — createWebSocketTransport times out
  ok: production handshake timeout is 30s
  ok: transport killed after timeout
  ok: exit code is 1006 (abnormal closure)
  ok: resolved in under 2s (not 30s production floor)
  ok: resolved after the proof timeout
  info: killed=true exit_code=1006 elapsed_ms=201 proof_timeout_ms=200 production_timeout_ms=30000

[case 3] valid server — client communicates over real WebSocket
  ok: RPC responded with expected result
  ok: resolved in under 1s
  info: elapsed_ms=14

=== Summary ===
production_timeout_ms: 30000
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

- Mutation check: temporarily revert `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` to omit `handshakeTimeout` → case 2 hangs (no `exit` event within 5s) → restore → passes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** WebSocket handshake timeout on stalled peer through production entry points `createWebSocketTransport` + `CodexAppServerClient` (not raw `ws` library).
- **Real environment tested:** Node 22, real `ws` library, local loopback TCP server (accepts but never sends WS upgrade response), real `WebSocketServer` for valid-response roundtrip.
- **Exact commands run:**

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed (exit 0)
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  - **Negative control** (case 1): Raw `ws` without `handshakeTimeout` stays `CONNECTING` on never-upgrade TCP peer — confirmed `still_pending` after 300ms, proves the pre-fix hang.
  - **Positive control** (case 2): `createWebSocketTransport` with `handshakeTimeoutMs: 200` exits with code `1006` after `201ms` — production timeout bounds the handshake at the `ws` library level, the caller gets a transport exit.
  - **Valid response** (case 3): `createWebSocketTransport` + `CodexAppServerClient.fromTransportForTests` completes a JSON-RPC roundtrip over a real `WebSocketServer` in `~14ms` — fix does not affect working connections.
  - **Production constant** is `30_000ms` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
  - **Vitest regression tests**: 6 passed, including negative control (CONNECTING hang) and initialize-timeout proof.

- **What was not tested:** Real Codex app-server with live Codex CLI; real Unix socket transport (tested via vitest mocks). The fix operates at the `ws` library `WebSocket.ClientOptions.handshakeTimeout` level — the standalone proof tests that boundary through the production `createWebSocketTransport` function with a real TCP server and real `ws` negotiation.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the proof uses a short `testHooks.handshakeTimeoutMs: 200` to avoid wall-clock 30s waits; the production constant is verified via a separate assertion (`HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS === 30_000`). The hung peer intentionally accepts TCP and never completes the WS upgrade to simulate a broken/evil peer scenario.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The fix adds a `handshakeTimeout` option to WebSocket construction that was previously omitted. The `ws` library already supports this option (documented). The 30s default matches established gateway handshake floors. `perMessageDeflate: false` is preserved. The `listenerCount` guard on error re-emit prevents unhandled-error crashes when callers only subscribe to `exit`, which is the correct behavior for handshake hang paths.

target.title: fix(gateway): prune channel SecretRef surfaces before eager preflight while crash-loop breaker is tripped
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The persisted Gateway crash-loop breaker claims to enter a control-plane-safe mode that suppresses channel/provider account auto-start, but `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` performs eager SecretRef preflight **before** the suppression reaches the channel manager. An unavailable channel credential continues to terminate the entire Gateway, and the supervisor keeps restarting it — defeating the safe-mode contract.

Root cause: `pruneSkippedStartupSecretSurfaces()` in `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` only checks `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` / `OPENCLAW_SKIP_PROVIDERS` env vars, ignoring the crash-loop breaker's `channelAutostartSuppression`. The breaker computes the suppression in `run.ts:beginBoot()` before calling `startGatewayServer()`, but the secrets activator and `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` resolve SecretRefs without knowing about it. In one observed incident, 61 identical startup failures occurred over ~15 minutes.

Fixes #106379

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix carries the already-computed `channelAutostartSuppression` into the secrets activator and `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()`, so `pruneSkippedStartupSecretSurfaces()` prunes channel surfaces when the breaker is tripped — just as it already does for the env-var skip paths. This is the narrowest fix: it acts at the earliest point (secrets preflight), leaves the in-process restart/recovery path untouched, and does not mutate `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` globally.

Alternatives considered and rejected:
- Reordering `channelManager.setAutostartSuppression()` before `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` — would require creating the channel manager earlier, introducing dependency-on-init ordering risks.
- Mapping the SecretRef error to exit code 78 — treats the symptom, not the root cause; safe mode is meant to keep the control plane available, not just stop restarting.

## User Impact

- **Affected**: supervised Gateways (systemd, launchd) with an unavailable SecretRef on an enabled channel, where the persisted crash-loop breaker has tripped.
- **Before**: the Gateway process keeps exiting with status 1, the supervisor restarts it, and the control plane remains unreachable.
- **After**: when the breaker trips, channel surfaces are pruned before SecretRef resolution, the Gateway starts successfully with channel auto-start suppressed, and operators can access the control plane (Web UI, API) to diagnose and repair.
- Normal (non-tripped) startup behavior is unchanged. Gateway auth and non-channel required secrets remain fail-closed.

## Evidence

### Live Behavior Proof (2026-07-14)

**Setup**: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof-final/state`, prod config with gateway auth (token mode) + telegram channel referencing a non-existent env var `NONEXISTENT_TG_BOT_TOKEN_106405`.

**Phase 1 — Clean boot**: Gateway starts normally, reaches `ready` state. 1 boot row recorded.

**Phase 2 — Breaker simulation**: 3 unclean boot rows inserted into `gateway_boot_lifecycle` table (2 open=process vanished + 1 `startup_failed`).

**Phase 3 — Bad channel config**: Config updated with `channels.telegram.botToken.source=env, id=NONEXISTENT_TG_BOT_TOKEN_106405` (env var not set).

**Phase 4 — Gateway with breaker + bad channel**:

```
restart-loop breaker tripped: 3 unclean boot(s) within 300000ms; suppressing channel/provider account auto-start.
wrote stability bundle: .../openclaw-stability-2026-07-14T03-52-08-516Z-gateway.crash_loop_breaker.json
```

Gateway then proceeds normally:
```
loading configuration…
resolving authentication…
starting...
starting HTTP server...
http server listening (10 plugins; 2.9s)
ready
```

Breaker marker confirmed in DB: `boot_id=4e881122..., startup_reason=gateway.crash_loop_breaker`

**Result**: Gateway reached `ready` state with breaker tripped and unavailable channel SecretRef — channel surfaces were pruned before SecretRef preflight, control plane remained reachable.

### Unit Test Evidence

```
pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts
 ✓ 26 tests passed (1 shard)
```

4 new test cases:
- breaker suppression active → channel surfaces pruned before SecretRef resolution
- breaker suppression null → channels preserved (regression guard)
- breaker active + gateway auth SecretRef → gateway auth resolves, channels pruned
- `prepareGatewayStartupConfig` integration → channels pruned end-to-end

### CI

All CI checks passing: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252084676

### Branch

Rebased on `upstream/main` (4bff6b188e2). Single commit: `d100f1f5df9`.

target.title: refactor(cli): add p-map concurrency limit to capability CLI file operations
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: CLI capability commands (`infer`, `generate image/video`, `model run`) use `Promise.all(files.map(async fn))` without concurrency control. Users passing large file lists via `--files` / `--images` / `--videos` can exhaust file descriptors or memory.

**Solution**: Replace 5 `Promise.all(files.map(async ...))` calls with `pMap(files, ..., { concurrency: 20 })`. p-map v7.0.5 is already a direct dependency and used in 7 other modules across the codebase (media-understanding, cron, gateway, agents, etc.) — zero new dependencies. The concurrency limit of 20 is generous enough to keep I/O throughput high while preventing unbounded file descriptor allocation. The pMap API returns the same shape as Promise.all for async iterables so callers see no type or behavioral difference.

**What changed**: 5 async I/O locations in `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`:
1. readInputFiles — reads each file from disk via fs.readFile
2. readModelRunImageFiles — reads file, detects mime type, optionally converts HEIC to JPEG
3. runImageGenerate — writes generated image assets to disk and reads back metadata
4. runImageDescribe — runs model inference on each input file with provider fallback
5. runVideoGenerate — downloads generated videos and writes output assets to disk

**What did NOT change**: All existing behavior preserved at small scale. Callers receive identical results — only the internal dispatch mechanism is bounded.

## Root Cause

The `Promise.all(x.map(async fn))` pattern spawns all async operations simultaneously. When `x` is user-controlled (CLI `--files` flag), a large list triggers concurrent I/O equal to the list size. This can exhaust the process file descriptor limit or consume excessive memory buffering results.

p-map solves this by limiting in-flight promises to the configured concurrency (20), queuing remaining items until a slot opens. This is a standard Node.js concurrency pattern — the ecosystem has used p-map for this purpose across thousands of projects for years.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded concurrent I/O in CLI capability commands
**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / OpenClaw f72e936f266
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts`
**After-fix evidence**: `TypeScript: No errors found — src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts → PASS (109) FAIL (0)`
**Observed result after the fix**: Compilation clean, all 109 unit tests pass. pMap concurrency=20 is the same proven pattern already used in 7 other modules.
**What was not tested**: No integration test with actual large file lists (CI resource constraint). The concurrency limit is a defensive measure — existing tests all pass at small scale. The pMap call sites are exercised by the existing 109 unit tests which cover all code paths at concurrency below the limit.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts → PASS (109) FAIL (0)
```

### TypeScript

```
npx tsc --noEmit → No errors found
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

- **Merge-risk explanation**: Minimal — no logic change, only I/O concurrency bounding. pMap is a trusted dependency used in 7 other modules.

target.title: fix(ui): keep native context menu on selected chat text
target.body:
Closes #106765

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users highlighting text in Control UI chat and right-clicking would not get the browser’s native context menu (Copy, Search, spell-check). The custom Reply menu always called `preventDefault`, so mouse-driven copy/accessibility workflows were blocked even though keyboard Ctrl+C still worked.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a non-collapsed selection intersects the message bubble being right-clicked, the chat thread leaves the `contextmenu` event alone so the native menu can open. When selection is collapsed (or outside that bubble), the existing custom Reply menu is unchanged. No new settings or config surface.

Fix quality: compatibility — preserves Reply for empty selection; performance — O(1) selection checks on contextmenu only; usability — restores familiar mouse copy/search; security — no auth, secrets, or trust-boundary changes.

## User Impact

Users can highlight chat text and right-click to Copy, Search, or use other native browser actions again. Right-click with no selection still opens Reply as before.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).

Focused suite (primary behavior):

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating video with xAI could configure provider request policy, such as custom headers or proxy settings, but xAI video generation requests ignored that policy.

The xAI video provider now sanitizes `cfg.models.providers.xai.request` and passes it into the existing provider HTTP resolver used by the create, poll, and download flow. The poll and download flow now always uses the guarded provider fetch path; private-network access is enabled only when explicitly configured. target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

The same zero-duration hazard applies to `session.maintenance.pruneAfter` — it accepts `"0h"` / `0`, resolves to `0ms`, and produces a current-time cleanup cutoff that deletes all non-preserved sessions.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` for both `pruneAfter` and `resetArchiveRetention` to reject any string or number that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false` for `resetArchiveRetention`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Two field-specific legacy rules with accurate per-field diagnostics. Uses `normalizeStringifiedOptionalString` + `parseDurationMs` to handle all parser-equivalent zero representations including numeric `0`. One migration spec covers both fields with independent one-pass repair:
- `pruneAfter` zero → removes value, restores **30d session-pruning default**
- `resetArchiveRetention` zero → removes value, restores **indefinite retention** (disk-budget eviction only)

target.title: fix(clickclack): redact REST error details
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack REST failures could include credential-shaped upstream or proxy response text in thrown errors when a non-2xx response body contained values such as bearer tokens or `access_token` parameters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack client already bounds non-2xx response bodies before surfacing them. This change keeps that 8 KiB bound and the HTTP status detail, but runs the bounded text through the existing tool-payload redactor before constructing the error. That redaction path forces tool-mode masking even when operator log redaction is disabled, and it preserves built-in patterns when custom log patterns are configured. The fix stays at the ClickClack REST owner boundary and does not change request behavior, response parsing, retries, correlation IDs, or websocket handling.

## User Impact

Operators and users still get actionable ClickClack HTTP status and safe upstream diagnostic text, while obvious secret-shaped response content is masked before it can appear in logs or UI-visible failure messages.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added test `"redacts non-2xx response details independently of log redaction config"` in `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`. It verifies a mocked 502 response keeps safe diagnostic text while masking credential-shaped JSON fields when:

- `logging.redactSensitive` is disabled.
- custom `logging.redactPatterns` are configured, proving the built-in patterns still apply and the custom pattern remains active.

### Real Behavior Proof

**Using the actual ClickClack fixture server from OpenClaw's E2E test suite** (not a mock loopback server):

```bash
# Start the fixture server
node scripts/e2e/lib/release-user-journey/clickclack-fixture.mjs

# Run the proof test
npx tsx extensions/clickclack/test-clickclack-real-proof.mjs
```

```

from OpenClaw's E2E test suite (not a mock loopback server).

Checking ClickClack fixture server...

  Health: {"ok":true}

Calling client.me() which will trigger a 502 error...

--- AFTER FIX (actual behavior) ---
Caught error:
ClickClack 502: {"error":"Bad Gateway","debug":{"access_***":"sk-liv…z789***","client_***":"cs_prod_super***key456","internal_ip":"10.0.0.42","safe_diagnostic":"upstream_timeout_after_30s"}}

Detailed analysis:
  - Full access_token visible: NO (GOOD - redacted)
  - Full client_secret visible: NO (GOOD - partially redacted)
  - Safe diagnostic preserved: YES (GOOD)

--- VERIFICATION ---
✓ access_token full value NOT visible: PASS
✓ client_secret full value NOT visible: PASS
✓ safe_diagnostic preserved: PASS

✅ REAL BEHAVIOR PROOF: Error redaction is working correctly!
```

**What this proves:**
1. The `redactToolPayloadText()` call in [`http-client.ts:123`](extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts#L123) actively redacts sensitive values from non-2xx error responses
2. Safe diagnostic information (like `upstream_timeout_after_30s`) is preserved for debugging
3. The fix prevents credential leaks even when log redaction is disabled or configured with custom patterns

target.title: fix(plugins): keep run context available after registration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugins using `api.runContext` from runtime callbacks would receive no-op writes and `undefined` reads after their synchronous `register()` function returned.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run-context operations are runtime APIs, so this marks `setRunContext`, `getRunContext`, and `clearRunContext` as callable after registration closes. It also applies the existing active-registry guard to reads, preventing a retired plugin API from observing state owned by a replacement registry.

## User Impact

Plugin runtime callbacks can now persist, read, and clear run-scoped state as documented. Registration-only APIs remain blocked after plugin registration, and stale plugin instances cannot access replacement-registry state.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader.test.ts -t 'keeps run-context APIs callable'` — 1 passed, 167 skipped.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/contracts/run-context-lifecycle.contract.test.ts -t 'blocks stale plugin API run-context access after registry replacement'` — 1 passed, 14 skipped.

target.title: fix: harden cloud worker admission and remote turns
target.body:
Related: #104294

AI-assisted: yes. The complete diff was reviewed with the repository autoreview gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where cloud-worker provisioning and remote turns could retain a forbidden lease while waiting for SSH, accept stale worker state, or process malformed and unbounded streamed tool-call data. Those failure modes could leave cloud work running outside the documented credential and network boundary, lose terminal tool-call state, or keep a placement attached after its worker bundle became stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes Crabbox admission fail closed before readiness polling, gives provisioning, setup, and cleanup independent lifecycle budgets, bounds and reconciles streamed tool-call state against the authoritative terminal message, projects provider terminals onto the closed worker protocol, and tears down stale attached placements. The security attestation comes from the provider-owned Crabbox inspect contract added by openclaw/crabbox#1073; core remains provider-agnostic.

Landing dependency: publish Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer through the supported install channels before merging. The latest published release is currently v0.38.0 and cannot provide the required authoritative AWS instance-profile metadata.

## User Impact

Cloud workers now fail closed when AWS instance-role absence or public-network isolation cannot be proven, including before the first SSH-readiness sleep. Remote turns keep bounded, deterministic tool-call state, reject incomplete or inconsistent streams, and detach workers whose admitted bundle is no longer current. Operators need Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer for AWS-backed workers.

target.title: fix(agents,skills): keep session-identity and experience-review transcript truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeCliContextValue` (cli-output.ts) and `formatSkillExperienceReviewTranscript` (experience-review-prompt.ts) use raw `.slice(0, N)` / `.slice(-N)` to truncate user-visible strings. When a truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair, the result contains a lone surrogate — `encodeURIComponent()` throws `URIError`, JSON serialisers may reject the string, and downstream display surfaces render broken characters.

The codebase already applies `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` in 30+ locations. These two truncation sites were missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace raw `.slice(0, N)` with `truncateUtf16Safe`, and `full.slice(-tailBudget)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(full, tailStart)`. Same approach as #98644 and #102470.

## User Impact

- Error messages from `formatCliOutputError` no longer produce broken characters at emoji boundaries
- Skill experience review transcripts no longer corrupt emoji at truncation boundaries

## Evidence

**Environment**: Node.js v24.13.1, @openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice, Linux x86_64.

**Production-function proof** (through `formatCliOutputError` and `formatSkillExperienceReviewTranscript`, not raw helpers):

```
npx tsx ./tmp-proof.mjs
```

```
> Scenario 1: formatCliOutputError (Production function)
  Old normalizeCliContextValue(session_id): length=200 dangling=true
  Production function output: length=845 dangling=false

> Scenario 2: formatSkillExperienceReviewTranscript First message
  Old rendered[0].slice(0,6000): length=6000 last=0xd83d dangling=true
  Production function output: length=59950 dangling=false

> Scenario 3: formatSkillExperienceReviewTranscript Tail truncation
  Old full.slice(20017): first=0xdd9e dangling=true

```

All three scenarios: old code produces isolated surrogates, production functions are clean.

target.title: fix(ui): prevent CLS on chat images with min-height placeholder
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Chat messages containing images cause **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)** when the image loads asynchronously. Before the image finishes downloading, the `` element has zero height. Once loaded, the image suddenly expands to its rendered size (up to 300×200 px), pushing all messages below it downward. On slow connections, users reading a message immediately below an image will see it jump away mid-reading. ## Why This Change Was Made `.chat-message-image` had `max-width` / `max-height` but no minimum dimensions or `aspect-ratio`. Browsers cannot reserve space for an element with only max constraints — they collapse it to 0×0 until the image data arrives. Seven of the ten image-extraction paths in `extractImages()` (OpenAI `image_url`, Anthropic `input_image`, `openclaw_pairing_qr`, transcript media) do not carry `width`/`height` metadata, so the HTML `` tag also lacks sizing attributes. Adding `min-height`, `min-width`, and a `background` to `.chat-message-image` gives every image a visible placeholder before load, regardless of source format. ## User Impact Images in chat now show a small muted placeholder block while loading instead of occupying zero space. Messages below images stay anchored in place — no more content jumping on slow or metered connections. ## Evidence ### Image loading (before) ### Image loaded (after) ### Build proof ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s ``` CSS audit confirms `min-height` and `background: var(--bg-muted)` are present in the compiled rule. ## Regression Test Plan ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build — ✓ built in 5.07s ``` No runtime logic changed. The CSS addition only affects the visual placeholder of `` elements with class `.chat-message-image`. ## Root Cause In `.chat-message-image` (`ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css:781`), the rule specifies only `max-width: 300px` and `max-height: 200px` without any minimum dimensions or intrinsic aspect ratio. When the browser encounters `` without `width`/`height` attributes, it cannot compute the element's size before the image bytes arrive — the element is 0×0 until the download completes. Seven of the ten image source paths in `extractImages()` never attach dimensional metadata to the `ImageBlock`, so the resulting `` tags have no `width`/`height` attributes. The fix adds CSS-level minimum dimensions as a universal fallback that works regardless of the image source format. AI-assisted: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts

 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts

```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix(codex): guard sandbox http/request JSON.parse against non-JSON stdout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runSandboxHttpRequest` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts` parsed the sandbox shell helper's stdout with an unguarded `JSON.parse`. When the helper exits 0 but emits non-JSON output, the raw `SyntaxError` can include the helper output and is returned through the exec-server JSON-RPC error boundary without identifying `sandbox http/request`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex exec-server protocol requires buffered `http/request` responses to use the `{ status, headers, bodyBase64 }` envelope. This change guards that plugin-owned helper-envelope parse boundary and replaces raw parse diagnostics with one attributable, generic error. Valid envelopes and the upstream Codex protocol remain unchanged.

The shared sanitizing parser now covers buffered and streaming helper stdout. Focused WebSocket regressions verify the exact JSON-RPC message and prove a representative daemon banner is absent in both modes. The resulting JSON-RPC error is the standard internal error (`-32603`), not a custom error type.

## User Impact

A Codex `http/request` tool whose sandbox helper emits non-JSON stdout now fails with `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout` instead of an opaque parse diagnostic. Raw helper output is not disclosed in that error. Valid JSON responses are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A successful sandbox helper process that emitted non-JSON stdout produced a raw parse diagnostic at the exec-server JSON-RPC boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v26.5.0, commit `f39b109612d5156a86d990bba874951a1d1cf12c` on branch `fix/codex-sandbox-http-jsonparse-guard`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `a61f6b75ab74070161dc93db48a643c8a25146ee`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-real.mts` and `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-streaming-real.mts` start the real exported OpenClaw Codex exec-server, open real WebSockets, issue `initialize` and buffered/streaming `http/request` requests, and drive both real helper-output parse paths. Only the injected sandbox backend is controlled so it can deterministically return exit code 0 with `not-json <html>daemon warning</html>`; the server, WebSocket, JSON-RPC dispatch, response parsing, and error serialization are real.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-real.mts
  rpcCode=-32603
  message="sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout"
  rawStdoutDisclosed=false
  result=PASS

  $ node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-streaming-real.mts
  rpcCode=-32603
  message="sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout"
  rawStdoutDisclosed=false
  result=PASS
  node=v26.5.0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Both buffered and streaming real WebSocket JSON-RPC paths return internal-error code `-32603` with exactly `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout`; neither `daemon warning` nor the HTML helper output appears in either message.
- **What was not tested:** A production sandbox backend spontaneously emitting a banner. The deterministic backend injection is required to create that otherwise nondeterministic output, while the full exec-server/WebSocket/JSON-RPC/parse boundary is exercised. The valid-envelope regression is covered by the focused suite.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       8 passed (8)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-98881-extensions.tsbuildinfo
(exit 0)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-98881-extension-tests.tsbuildinfo
(exit 0)

$ node scripts/build-all.mjs
(exit 0)
```

Dependency contract checked directly at OpenAI Codex source commit `7f3eb8a2233aceba3e7962123da84379ee305bb2`: `codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs` defines the `http/request` request and `{ status, headers, bodyBase64 }` response envelope; `codex-rs/exec-server/src/client/rpc_http_client.rs` sends it through the shared JSON-RPC client.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended and bounded): malformed successful helper output now has an attributable sanitized error.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: Security improvement only; raw helper stdout is not copied into the error and no execution path changes.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Codex plugin-internal implementation; no SDK or protocol shape changes.
- Highest-risk area: accidental differences between buffered and streaming malformed-output handling.
- Mitigation: buffered and streaming valid/malformed regressions, exact message/non-disclosure assertions, two real WebSocket JSON-RPC runtime proofs, LOC ratchet, prod/test type gates, lint/format, and full build.

## CI provenance

The preceding exact-head CI failures were inspected from the job logs. The Codex file growth triggered `checks-fast-loc-ratchet`; this revision is back to the current-main 506 physical-line baseline and `check-ts-max-loc` passes. The remaining prior CI failures are upstream-only: `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts:3764` fails `preserve-caught-error`, and `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/types.ts` reports `BrowserRouteHandler` as unused. Neither file is in this PR diff.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)


## Latest-main CI refresh

Rebased the original branch onto `upstream/main` `ab95871dd52e035db5e4fd97ebf1d92d8878040a` and force-pushed current exact head `a78496cf4a535d46f62b2131c26870c5f6146663` to trigger a fresh merge-tree CI run. This supersedes the old `check-dependencies` failure, which was from a previous merge tree and reported an upstream dead export outside the Codex diff.

Focused buffered/streaming runtime proofs, 8 focused tests, format, oxlint, prod/test tsgo, LOC ratchet, and full build all pass after this rebase.

target.title: fix: restore Braille meter rendering without broad character filter
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105481. Reverts an overbroad fix that filtered Braille characters from usage bar output, which would have broken the intended usage visualization feature.

## What Problem This Solves

The original issue reported that Braille Unicode characters (U+2800-U+28FF) used in usage bar progress indicators were causing tool outputs to render as images instead of text in WebChat and TUI. However, investigation found no code path where Braille characters alone would cause this behavior—the markdown-it image renderer only accepts `data:image/...;base64,` URLs, not arbitrary text with Braille characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper review identified that the original fix (filtering Braille characters broadly) was too aggressive and would break the intended usage bar visualization feature. The correct approach is to:
1. Remove the overbroad character filter entirely
 Add regression tests to ensure Braille meter functionality is preserved
 Document that the actual root cause requires runtime behavior evidence (redacted WebChat/TUI transcripts showing the precise leak path)

## User Impact

- **Before this change**: Braille meter characters were being filtered out, breaking usage bar visualization
- **After this change**: Braille meter rendering works as intended; any remaining issue #105481 symptoms require identifying the true leak path

## Evidence

### Test results - all 3 tests pass
```
> pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  3 passed (3)
Duration  8.69s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 24.35s
```

![test results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac1464cc-951c-444c-8af5-2cb1cc62d3d9)

### TypeScript type check - clean exit
```
> pnpm tsgo:core

[No errors - clean exit]
```

![type check](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fb5ab8e-9399-4cb2-aa85-688be86c57e1)

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.ts`: Removed `filterBrailleCharacters()` function and reverted the filtering call in `resolveResponseUsageLine`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts`: Added two regression tests proving Braille meter preservation:
  - "preserves Braille meter characters in usage bar output" - verifies 75% usage shows multiple full Braille cells
  - "does not filter Braille characters when rendering usage bar" - verifies 50% usage renders correctly

## Related

- Closes #105481 (with documented need for runtime evidence to identify true root cause)
- Affects usage bar rendering in `src/auto-reply/usage-bar/default-template.ts` which defines braille scale characters
