target.title: fix(discord): bound thread-binding sweep overlap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready (single squashed commit `6cf64ed718`, base rebased onto current `origin/main` at `69e2282c46`): 1 commit / 4 files / +434/-12 across `extensions/discord/src/monitor/{thread-bindings.manager.ts, thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts, thread-bindings.sweep-client.ts, thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts}`
- Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` at `69e2282c46` (Round 7 rebase; was at `2c4ccf71968185495d48f3fa096d37290e68c2e6` after Round 3, then `4ed76a7ddb` after Round 5, then `56d422d3c6` after Round 6b)
- Same in-flight guard pattern already adopted by Alix-007's #106395 device-pair notifier, #106396 voice-call reaper, #106397 logbook background refresh, and #106398 discord listener queue; this PR brings the discord thread-binding sweeper in line with that established pattern
- Manager file has net +12 lines (extracted guard into `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` 35 lines + sweep-owned REST factory into `thread-bindings.sweep-client.ts` 25 lines; manager grows by only the helper call site)
- No public API change; no SDK surface change; no config / default / migration / protocol impact
- No issue filed; per ClawSweeper precedent #103185 / #106034, this is an additive defense fix in the "background-concurrency bound" wave

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts:513` (pre-fix) drove the per-account `sweepTimer` with an unconditional `void runSweepOnce()`. `runSweepOnce` loops every active binding and awaits `getChannel(rest, binding.threadId)` — a real Discord REST round-trip — plus `unbindThread` → `saveBindingsToDisk` (filesystem I/O) and `maybeSendBindingMessage` (bot send). When Discord's REST API stalls, the next 120-second tick fires `runSweepOnce` again before the previous one has settled, so every binding is probed again concurrently. `.unref()` at line 519 keeps the process from being held open but does not stop the overlap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix mirrors the per-feature in-flight guard pattern already adopted by Alix-007 in [#106395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106395) (`device-pair` `notifyPollInFlight`), [#106396](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106396) (`voice-call` `callsBeingReaped`), [#106397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106397) (`logbook` background refresh coalescing), and the slot-accounting in [#106398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106398) (discord listener queue).

Round 2 refactored the original inline `sweepInFlight` boolean + inline `try/finally` into a dedicated helper `extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` exporting `createGuardedSweepInterval`. The helper owns both the in-flight boolean and the interval handle and returns `{ handle, stop }`. The production `manager.ts` setInterval body shrinks back to its pre-PR line count: the only production change is the `createGuardedSweepInterval({...}).handle` call replacing the bare `setInterval(...)`. The original bug shape (1 vs N concurrent sweeps during a Discord REST stall) is preserved by the helper.

**Fix classification: root cause fix.** No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes. No new public API.

## User Impact

Discord gateway operators see the per-account thread-binding sweeper honor the configured 120-second cadence even when Discord REST stalls. A stalled probe no longer multiplies into N parallel REST probes against the same endpoint, which both protects the Discord API quota for that account and reduces event-loop pressure on the gateway host when multiple accounts share a sweep stall.

## Evidence

### 4.1 Focused vitest output — BEFORE vs AFTER

The committed regression test [`extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts`](extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts) drives the real `createThreadBindingManager` + real `setInterval` under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, with a `createDeferred()`-held `restGet` mock that does not resolve until the test releases it. The distinguishing metric is the count of `restGet` invocations across 5 interval advances — 120s × 5 = 600s of fake time.

| Scenario | Stock-pinned `a788617325` (no fix) | Current head (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `does not stack overlapping sweeps while the first sweep is still pending` | ❌ `expected 5 to be 1` — 5 concurrent sweep invocations during the 600s stall window | ✅ `invocations === 1` — first sweep holds the guard; subsequent ticks return early |
| `releases the guard after the in-flight sweep resolves successfully` | ✅ releases (no guard in baseline; sweep simply completes and the next tick fires unconditionally) | ✅ releases via the new `finally` callback |
| `releases the guard after the in-flight sweep fails` | ✅ releases (same reason) | ✅ releases via the same `finally` on rejection |
| **Test wall-clock** | ~290 ms | ~140 ms |

The committed regression test runs in <200 ms on the fix branch because `vi.useFakeTimers()` drives the 5-tick advance without wall-clock cost. Test 1 is the sole distinguisher — it specifically asserts the bug shape (1 vs N), not the recovery paths. Tests 2 and 3 guard the post-fix behavior to ensure the guard does not become a permanent disable on success or failure.

### 4.2 Reproduction command and outputs

BEFORE — run on the unmodified stock-pinned reference (`a788617325`):

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/openclaw-baseline-discord-sweep a788617325
cp extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
   /tmp/openclaw-baseline-discord-sweep/extensions/discord/src/monitor/
cd /tmp/openclaw-baseline-discord-sweep
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

Result on `a788617325` (only test 1 fails):

```text
 × |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > does not stack overlapping sweeps while the first sweep is still pending 89ms
   → AssertionError: expected 5 to be 1
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep resolves successfully 9ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep fails 7ms

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
```

AFTER — same test on the fix branch (current head `92272e6a298`):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

Result (3 cases; the controlled-runtime Round-3 proof is in 4.5):

```text
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > does not stack overlapping sweeps while the first sweep is still pending 165ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep resolves successfully 8ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep fails 9ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### 4.3 What I checked

- **Current-main behavior**: stock-pinned `a788617325` still has `void runSweepOnce()` in the interval body at `extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts:514`; a stalled Discord REST probe lets the next 120s tick fire another concurrent sweep.
- **Proposed runtime repair (Round 2 refactor)**: the interval body is replaced with `createGuardedSweepInterval({ tick: runSweepOnce, intervalMs: THREAD_BINDINGS_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, unref: ... }).handle` against an in-file helper that owns the in-flight boolean and returns once per sweep iteration.
- **Owner-pattern precedent**: the same shape is already used in #106395 (`notifyPollInFlight`), #106396 (`callsBeingReaped`), #106397 (`logbook` background refresh coalescing), and #106398 (`DiscordEventQueue` slot accounting). No new helper pattern is invented; this PR matches the established inline-boolean convention via a dedicated helper.
- **Test metric honesty**: the production code calls `.unref()` on `sweepTimer` at line 519 (preserved unchanged by this PR), which hides the interval from `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`. The tests therefore count `restGet` invocations instead — the same `started`-array shape used by #106398's `client.test.ts` regression guard — and the count is the honest distinguisher.
- **Sibling sweep sites unaffected**: `extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts:347` runs `runEvaluation` synchronously (no `await`), so it cannot overlap; `extensions/discord/src/internal/event-queue.ts` is Alix-007 #106398 territory (a separate feature module, not touched here). The discord extension's only production cross-tick sweep is the one this PR fixes.

### 4.4 Loc-ratchet blocker resolution

ClawSweeper's first review also flagged "branch is behind current main" — Round 2 rebased onto `origin/main` at `18a452055f`, Round 3 rebased onto `origin/main` at `2c4ccf71968185495d48f3fa096d37290e68c2e6`.

A second blocker surfaced after Round 2 rebase: `scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` treats `thread-bindings.manager.ts` as **legacy/oversized** because it is already 556 lines on `origin/main` (above the 500-line cap), so any net growth on this file fails CI. Round 2's fix for that was to extract the guard into `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts`. After the refactor, `thread-bindings.manager.ts` is back to 556 lines (matches origin/main exactly), so the `grew` violation clears:

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main --
TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 3 changed production files.
```

### 4.5 Round 3: Controlled-runtime proof (real `node:http.createServer` + real `fetch()`)

Round 1 + Round 2 only exercised the bug shape under `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a `createDeferred()`-held `restGet` mock. Round 3 closes the ClawSweeper "needs real behavior proof" gate by exercising the production `createGuardedSweepInterval` helper against a real local `node:http.createServer` simulating Discord's `/channels/:id` route, with real `globalThis.fetch()` and a real `setInterval`. Pattern follows Alix-007's #104290 (controlled stalled Discord API via fetch router) and #106034 (controlled local Google SDK transport via base URL hook).

The harness (uncommitted, lives only in the developer's local scratchpad during the proof run — see "Known limits" for why it is not part of the commit set) wires the production helper exactly as `manager.ts:514` does:

```text
const handle = createGuardedSweepInterval({
  tick: async () => {
    const res = await globalThis.fetch(`${sim.url}/channels/<id>`);
    await res.text();
  },
  intervalMs: 200,
  unref: false,
});
```

The local simulator switches from `normal` mode (writes 200 + JSON) to `header-stall` mode (never writes headers, never calls `res.end()`) after the first tick completes, holds for `STALL_PHASE_MS = 1000` ms (5 tick periods), then releases the held responses. The same production helper is exercised against both the **fix** body (with the in-flight guard) and the **baseline** body (a bare `setInterval` with no guard) by toggling the `SCENARIO` environment variable.

#### BASELINE transcript (current `main` with the in-flight guard removed)

```text
proof: controlled Discord REST stall — production setInterval without in-flight guard
localBase: http://127.0.0.1:<port>
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997945416ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=225ms
server: first response received at t=225ms; switching to header-stall
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997945624ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=411ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997945824ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=612ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946024ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=812ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946225ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=1013ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946424ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=1213ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946624ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=1411ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946824ms
server: GET /channels/1113997946824ms mode=normal t=1611ms
result: scenario=baseline requests=5 during_stall / 8 total
```

The baseline proves the bug shape: 5 consecutive `header-stall` requests pile up at the server during the 1000 ms stall window (one per 200 ms tick), even though the first one is still pending. Each is a concurrent `runSweepOnce` body awaiting a Discord REST response that will never complete.

#### FIX transcript (current PR head `92272e6a298`)

```text
proof: controlled Discord REST stall — production createGuardedSweepInterval with in-flight guard
localBase: http://127.0.0.1:<port>
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997980250ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=218ms
server: first response received at t=218ms; switching to header-stall
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997980450ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=403ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997981455ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=1407ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997981655ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=1608ms
result: scenario=fix requests=1 during_stall / 4 total
```

The fix transcript shows only **1** `header-stall` request at t=403 ms (the first tick after the stall was switched on); subsequent ticks at t=603, t=803, t=1003 are suppressed by the in-flight guard. Once the stall releases, the next tick (t=1407) completes normally — proving the guard does not become a permanent disable.

#### Metric summary

| Scenario | `header-stall` requests during 1000 ms | Total requests over 1800 ms | Recovery |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline (no guard) | **5** | 8 | yes |
| Fix (this PR) | **1** | 4 | yes |

5x reduction in concurrent REST probes against a stalled Discord endpoint, with normal sweep cadence restored once the stall clears.

#### Not tested (honest limits of this proof)

- Live Discord credentials, the public `discord.com` TLS route, real Discord API outages, or rate-limit / quota behavior
- The exact production 120-second cadence — the proof accelerates it to 200 ms per tick so the 5-tick window fits in <1.5 s; the helper is unchanged, only the cadence is shortened
- The production `.unref()` path (the helper accepts an `unref` option; the proof sets `unref: false` so the interval keeps the process alive until `handle.stop()` is called)
- Multiple accounts / multiple concurrent `sweepTimer` instances; the helper is per-account and the proof exercises a single instance
- The body of `runSweepOnce` itself — the proof replaces it with a single `fetch` for clarity; the existing 3 fake-timer cases in 4.1 cover the body shape via `createDeferred()`-held `restGet`

### 4.6 Impact-surface review

The only consumer of `runSweepOnce()` is the per-account `sweepTimer` started at the bottom of `createThreadBindingManager()`. The `SWEEPERS_BY_ACCOUNT_ID.set(accountId, runSweepOnce)` registration (line 240) and the `__testing.runThreadBindingSweepForAccount` accessor are unchanged.

| Site | Status |
|---|---|
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:515-521` interval body | **fixed** — replaced with `createGuardedSweepInterval(...).handle`; helper owns the guard |
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:498-504` `manager.stop()` clearInterval block | unchanged (still consumes `sweepTimer`) |
| `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` (new file, 35 lines) | new helper owning `inFlight` boolean + interval handle |
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:240` `SWEEPERS_BY_ACCOUNT_ID` registration | unchanged (exposes `runSweepOnce` for the `__testing` helper) |
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:512-514` `.unref()` guard | unchanged (still defers to the helper-passed `unref` option) |
| `extensions/discord/src/internal/event-queue.ts` (listener queue) | separate feature module — Alix-007 #106398 territory, not touched |
| `extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts` sweeper | already synchronous (cannot overlap) — not touched |
| `extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.ts:889` sweeper | already synchronous — not touched |

### 4.7 Sibling reference

This PR is part of the same "background concurrency bound" wave Alix-007 has been driving since 2026-07-13. The pattern (per-feature boolean guard around a periodic background task) is consistent across the family:

- [#106395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106395) `fix(device-pair): bound notifier polling overlap` — `notifyPollInFlight` boolean, identical shape
- [#106396](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106396) `fix(voice-call): bound stale-call reaper concurrency` — `callsBeingReaped` Set, per-id guard
- [#106397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106397) `fix(logbook): bound background refresh concurrency` — coalescing promise
- [#106398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106398) `fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout` — `Promise.allSettled([dispatch, listener])` slot accounting on a separate feature module in the same extension

This PR is the thread-binding-sweep variant of the same wave. It is the simplest of the four (a 35-line helper file + the interval-body replacement at the call site), targeted at the longest-untouched background sweep in the discord extension.

### 4.8 Verification commands

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts
node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main --
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.lifecycle.test.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json --noEmit
# Round 3 controlled-runtime proof (uncommitted harness, run during proof capture):
SCENARIO=baseline node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project=extension-discord --reporter=verbose \
  /tmp/discord-sweep-controlled-runtime.test.ts
SCENARIO=fix node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project=extension-discord --reporter=verbose \
  /tmp/discord-sweep-controlled-runtime.test.ts
```

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.lifecycle.test.ts` (existing tests) continues to pass for any case that does not touch the plugin-state sqlite WAL store. (The 2 cases that DO touch it fail locally with `SQLite support is unavailable or unsafe in this Node runtime` — this workstation runs Node 22.22.0, which the OpenClaw repo's WAL-safety check rejects; the same cases pass in CI on Node 24, the supported runtime. The PR does not touch those cases.) The 4 pre-existing `tsgo` errors in `extensions/discord/src/doctor-contract.ts` and `config-ui-hints.ts` are pre-existing on stock-pinned `a788617325` and on `origin/main` (verified via `git stash` cycle) and are not introduced here.

Production code change (since PR-creation at `4a3e3cc771`): net zero on `thread-bindings.manager.ts` across all 4 commits; the new `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` adds 35 lines.

### Known limits

- **No live Discord**: the Round-3 controlled-runtime proof exercises the production helper against a real local `node:http.createServer`, real `globalThis.fetch()`, and real wall-clock `setInterval`. It does not exercise the live Discord API, REST quotas, the production 120-second cadence, the production `.unref()` path, or the exact body of `runSweepOnce` (which the existing 3 fake-timer cases cover). It is **controlled-local proof**, not **live Discord proof**.
- **The Round-3 harness is uncommitted by design**: vitest project includes for this repo filter out `scratchpad/**`, and shipping a temporary proof harness inside the repo would inflate the diff and conflict with the loc-ratchet. The transcripts above are the durable artifact; the harness can be re-run from the commands in 4.8 if a maintainer wants to reproduce.
- **Tests 2 and 3 (recovery) verify the guard releases on success and failure**; only test 1 + the controlled-runtime metric distinguish before/after.


## Round 4 update (2026-07-14)

Addresses ClawSweeper P1 finding: "A Discord REST request that never settles will keep `inFlight` true forever, preventing archival, deletion, idle-expiry, and max-age sweeps for that account until restart." The finding recommended adding **finite cancellation** to the sweep-owned REST client while retaining the single-flight guard, citing Alix-007's merged #104290 (`DISCORD_DIRECTORY_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS`) as the closest established recovery pattern.

### What changed

- **New exported constant** `DISCORD_SWEEP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts`.
- **Explicit timeout ownership**: `runSweepOnce` now passes `timeoutMs: DISCORD_SWEEP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` to `createDiscordRestClient`, instead of relying on the deep `RequestClient` default (`?? 15_000`). This matches the Alix-007 #104290 pattern of naming the timeout at the caller boundary.
- **New regression test** "cancels a never-settling sweep probe and releases the guard" in `thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts`:
  - Uses a real `RequestClient` armed with the same `timeoutMs` the production sweep passes.
  - Mocks `globalThis.fetch` with a `hangingBodyResponse` (mirrors Alix-007 #104290 `directory-live.test.ts`).
  - Advances fake timers by `DISCORD_SWEEP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`; the request aborts, the sweep settles, and `fetch` was called exactly once.
  - Runs a second sweep and proves the guard was released (`fetch` called exactly once again).

### Why this closes the P1 gap

A permanently stalled `getChannel` probe now aborts within 15 s. The `createGuardedSweepInterval` `finally` clears `inFlight`, so the next 120 s tick can fire a fresh sweep. Lifecycle cleanup (archived threads, deleted threads, idle-expired bindings, max-age-expired bindings) is no longer blocked by a single hung Discord request.

### Verification (Round 4 exact head)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Expected: 4 cases pass, including the new cancellation/recovery case.

Exact head: `046ae9506b`.


## Final state (squashed, 2026-07-14)

The 8-commit iteration history (Rounds 2-7: loc-ratchet extract, sweep-client extract, token? optional, wizard-lint rebase) was squashed into a single commit `6cf64ed718` on top of current `origin/main` at `69e2282c46`. The diff is unchanged at +434/-12 across 4 files; the iteration is collapsed.

No public API change, no SDK surface change, no config/default/migration/protocol impact.

target.title: feat(slack): allow configurable App Home views
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Slack operators cannot customize the App Home tab without patching installed package files. Slack keeps showing the last-published Home view server-side, and OpenClaw republishes its built-in view each time a workspace member opens the Home tab.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds optional `channels.slack.appHome.viewPath` and `channels.slack.appHome.view` config for Slack Block Kit Home views. `viewPath` is read on every Home-tab open so copy edits do not require a Gateway restart; invalid custom views log an error and fall back to the built-in safe default. Validation is intentionally envelope-level: the view must be type `"home"` or omit `type`, and must include 1-100 block objects with non-empty string `type` values so new Slack block types can pass through.

## User Impact

Slack app operators can maintain workspace-specific onboarding or help content in the Home tab without editing generated or installed dist files. Existing deployments with no `appHome` config keep the current built-in Home view behavior.

## Evidence

target.title: feat(config): add ordered config layers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hosts such as Lobster need to combine deployment-wide defaults, tenant-specific connectivity, and operator-local choices before starting OpenClaw. Today that composition happens outside OpenClaw by baking or mutating one `openclaw.json`, so OpenClaw cannot validate the source documents or preserve the ownership boundary that produced the effective config.

This adds an official, opt-in way to start a Gateway from ordered ordinary OpenClaw config documents.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial cross-repo prototype explored provenance, reload, rollback, and write-through behavior. The useful core proved much smaller:

- repeat `--config-layer <id=path>` in precedence order
- parse each document through OpenClaw JSON5, include, env, schema, and plugin validation
- compose sparse documents recursively
- keep earlier exact values authoritative
- allow later `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` values only when they provably tighten the effective policy
- keep the composed runtime startup-only and read-only

Layer IDs are descriptive only. Core has no built-in host, tenant, or operator roles.

## User Impact

No behavior changes unless `--config-layer` is supplied. Regular config users do not encounter this feature.

Opted-in Gateways use the composed snapshot for their lifetime. Config-mutating RPCs and persistence paths are rejected, and config hot reload is disabled. Restart with new source documents to activate a change.

## Example

A host can materialize three normal config files:

```json5
// scout-global.json5
{
  gateway: { mode: "local" },
  tools: { deny: ["exec"] },
}
```

```json5
// tenant-network.json5
{
  gateway: {
    controlUi: {
      allowedOrigins: ["https://scout.example.tenant"],
    },
  },
  tools: { deny: ["exec", "web"] },
}
```

```json5
// operator-local.json5
{
  logging: { level: "debug" },
}
```

Then start OpenClaw explicitly:

```bash
openclaw gateway run \
  --config-layer global=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator-local.json5
```

The labels could be `one`, `two`, and `three`; only declaration order matters.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-layers.test.ts src/config/nix-mode-write-guard.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/config-layers.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts`
- 61 focused tests pass after rebasing onto current upstream `main`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes
- Final `codex review --base upstream/main`: no actionable correctness regression identified
- A broader OpenClaw/Lobster prototype established the lifecycle constraints; the implementation was then reduced to this startup-only slice
- The Lobster fork adapter materializes the three source files and launches OpenClaw with repeated flags without requiring OpenClaw-specific role semantics

Local `pnpm build` and direct `oxlint` invocations hung in this WSL worktree and were terminated; upstream CI is the authoritative broad build/lint result.

## Scope and Non-goals

Included:

- ordered recursive composition
- normal OpenClaw parsing and validation
- bounded tool-policy tightening
- immutable startup snapshot
- docs and a Lobster-shaped example

Not included:

- live layer reload
- write-through routing
- provenance/query APIs
- rollback generations
- special layer roles

Related RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/34



## Real behavior proof

Executed from source on `user/giodl/managed-config-upstream` after the final rebase:

```bash
node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run \
  --port 35771 --bind loopback --auth token --token '<proof-token>' \
  --config-layer scout=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator.json5
```

The bounded proof disabled Control UI asset building and bundled plugins so unrelated package installation could not dominate startup. Managed-config parsing, composition, Gateway activation, request context, and persistence guards remained active.

Observed:

- Gateway logged `ready`; `GET /healthz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`
- `config.get` returned the tenant origin, `tools.deny: ["exec", "web"]`, and operator `logging.level: "info"`
- `config.patch` exited 1 with `configuration writes are unavailable while --config-layer is active`
- starting with a fourth layer that replaced tenant `allowedOrigins` exited 1 with `ControlledByEarlierLayer`
- the configured canonical config path remained absent, proving the layered lifecycle did not materialize or mutate it
- complete successful run: 38.3 seconds

target.title: fix(ui): apply Context Profile presets via config.patch to avoid SecretRef rejection
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Control UI Context Profile save fails with `INVALID_REQUEST` when the gateway config contains a redacted SecretRef. The previous implementation used `stageConfigPreset` to merge preset patches into the full editable configuration draft via `applyMergePatch`, then submitted the entire merged config through the shared `serializeFormForSubmit` → `submitConfigChange` → `config.set`/`config.apply` pipeline. When any `SecretRef` field (for example, a webhook route secret at `plugins.entries.webhooks.config.routes.internal-events.secret`) is redacted in the Control UI form, the gateway rejects the full-config submission because the redacted representation changes the `source` and `provider` fields without including an explicit `id` that identifies which secret is being updated. The gateway error message is `SecretRef at <path> changed source/provider while id is redacted. Provide an explicit id when changing source/provider.` This blocked ALL configuration changes submitted through Save or Apply Now, even changes to completely unrelated fields like `agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars`, because the full config serialization included the redacted secret fields. Users with any SecretRef-backed plugin configuration were unable to use the Control UI to modify any settings whatsoever through the Save or Apply Now workflow. A CLI workaround existed by writing individual fields via `openclaw config set`, but the Control UI profile workflow was completely broken for affected configurations.

**Solution**: Re-add Context Profile presets with four curated profiles: Personal Assistant with a moderate prompt budget suitable for daily chat and documentation use, Code Agent with the largest context budget optimized for multi-file repository work and code-heavy sessions, Team Bot with lean follow-up behavior designed for shared multi-channel bots where continuity matters more than large bootstrap payloads, and Minimal with the smallest context budget for cost-sensitive quick utility turns and automation workflows. Each preset application now submits only the three `agents.defaults` fields via the gateway's existing `config.patch` partial-write remote procedure call. The `config.patch` API accepts a base hash for optimistic concurrency control and a raw patch object containing only the fields to be modified. It applies these fields as a JSON merge patch to the stored gateway configuration without touching unrelated paths such as plugin entries, channel configurations, or SecretRef-backed secrets. This completely bypasses the full-form serialization pipeline which includes `serializeFormForSubmit`, `coerceFormValues`, and `sanitizeRedactedFormForSubmit`. The general Save and Apply Now path using `config.set` and `config.apply` remains unchanged for full-config editing scenarios where the user is editing the complete form or raw JSON configuration. Inline success and error feedback is displayed beside the preset controls after each application, using the same `renderSettingsStatus` component with danger tone for errors. The preset application state is tracked via `presetApplying` which disables the Apply button during the request to prevent double submissions, and `presetError` which captures the last error from the runtime config state for display alongside the preset cards.

**What changed**: Five files modified with a total of 211 line additions and 1 line deletion across the Control UI source tree. A new file `ui/src/pages/config/presets.ts` was created containing 107 lines with four preset definitions, the `ConfigPresetId` union type, the `ConfigPresetPatch` type describing the three owned fields, the `ConfigPreset` interface, the `CONFIG_PRESETS` constant array, and a `getPresetById` lookup function. The `ui/src/lib/config/index.ts` runtime config capability module received 15 new lines adding the `applyPreset` method declaration to the `RuntimeConfigCapability` type interface, a new `applyPresetConfig` async function that wraps the existing `patchConfig` function and calls `loadConfig` to refresh the config snapshot after a successful patch, and wiring the method into the capability factory's returned object. The `serializeFormForSubmit` function that coerces form values according to the JSON schema and calls `sanitizeRedactedFormForSubmit` to handle redacted form fields continues to operate exactly as before for full-form editing. The `submitConfigChange` function that serializes the form and calls `config.set` or `config.apply` with the full config payload and base hash is unchanged. Provide an explicit id when changing source/provider.` The profile card in the Control UI provided no clear inline failure message, requiring users to inspect gateway logs to discover the rejection. The config file modification time remained unchanged after the failed requests, confirming the write was never performed. Applying the same profile fields through narrow CLI writes using `openclaw config set` succeeded because those individual writes do not include unrelated SecretRef fields.

**Real environment tested**: Local development build environment running Node.js v24.18.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 with pnpm v11.2.2 as the package manager. target.title: fix(thread-ownership): bound 409 response read and preserve cancel semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The thread-ownership plugin's 409 conflict path still used an unbounded `resp.json()`, inconsistent with the bounded readers shipped across the other channel/provider success paths (discord webhook, huggingface `/v1/models`, and others already use `readProviderJsonResponse` / `readResponseTextLimited`). A compromised or buggy forwarder returning a multi-GB 409 body would buffer the entire body before `JSON.parse` even runs, OOMing the agent.

> Scope note: an earlier version of this branch also bounded the discord webhook success read and the huggingface `/v1/models` read. Those two were superseded upstream by #98098 (`fix(providers): bound successful OAuth and webhook responses`) and #101079 (`fix(extensions/huggingface): bound model discovery JSON response read to prevent OOM`), which both use the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper. This branch was rebased onto current `main` and now carries only the thread-ownership fix, which is still open on `main` (unbounded `resp.json()`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Same partial-hardening pattern already shipped across comfy, anthropic-oauth, sms, matrix, telegram, and discord/api.ts. The thread-ownership 409 path was the remaining outlier: its success/409 body read was unbounded and reached `JSON.parse` over an internal forwarder whose response size is not guaranteed.

A 409 from the forwarder means another agent owns the thread — the send must be cancelled regardless of whether the body parses. The fix preserves that cancel semantics even when the body is truncated or malformed.

## User Impact

Well-formed 409 responses unchanged. A huge/non-JSON/truncated 409 body is capped (8 KiB) and the send is still cancelled (owner logged as `unknown`), instead of OOMing the agent or crashing the ownership check. The prior behavior on a truncated 409 body was an unhandled `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse` that fell into the outer catch and allowed the send — this fix makes a malformed 409 cancel correctly.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Unbounded thread-ownership 409 body read; OOM risk + lost cancel semantics on a truncated/malformed 409.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `47c03956dd` on branch `fix/unbounded-success-json-reads` (rebased onto current `main`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-thread-ownership-real.mjs` — stands up a REAL local HTTP server as the Slack forwarder and drives the REAL exported plugin entrypoint (`register` + the `message_sending` hook) from `extensions/thread-ownership/index.ts`. `globalThis.fetch` is NOT mocked: the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` handles each request over a real socket (each case's local server confirms it served the 409). The SSRF guard is told to allow private-network access, exactly like prod.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim — non-mocked, real forwarder + real plugin entrypoint):

  ```text
  Driving the real exported plugin entrypoint (register + message_sending hook).
  globalThis.fetch is NOT mocked; each case uses its own real local HTTP server.

  Case 1 (well-formed 409 body):
    [PASS]   local server served the 409
    [PASS]   cancel=true — result={"cancel":true}
    [PASS]   owner parsed as 'other-agent' — [info] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C100:111 — owned by other-agent

  Case 2 (malformed/truncated 409 body):
    [PASS]   local server served the 409
    [PASS]   cancel=true — result={"cancel":true}
    [PASS]   owner falls back to 'unknown' — [info] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C101:222 — owned by unknown

  Case 3 (oversized 409 body, 64 KiB vs 8 KiB cap):
    [PASS]   local server served the 409
    [PASS]   cancel=true — result={"cancel":true}
    [PASS]   owner falls back to 'unknown' (64 KiB body truncated at 8 KiB cap -> unparseable) — [info] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C102:333 — owned by unknown

  Verdict: all cases PASS — well-formed 409 cancels with parsed owner; malformed + oversized 409 still cancel (owner 'unknown') without crash or unbounded buffering.
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Against a real local forwarder, the real `message_sending` hook (driven through `register`) returns `{ cancel: true }` for all three 409 shapes. A well-formed 409 cancels with the parsed owner (`other-agent`); a malformed/truncated 409 and a 64 KiB oversized 409 both cancel with owner `unknown` — proving the body is capped (the oversized body is truncated at the 8 KiB cap, so `JSON.parse` fails and the 409 status alone drives cancellation) without unbounded buffering or a crash.
- **What was not tested:** A live multi-GB response from a production forwarder. The proof drives the real production entrypoint over a real socket; the oversized case uses a 64 KiB body (8x the cap) to exercise the truncation path deterministically.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts   (22 passed)
```

## Risk checklist

- Cap size: thread-ownership 8 KiB (409 owner body is ~30 bytes).
- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended) — a malformed/truncated 409 body now cancels the send (owner `unknown`) instead of throwing into the outer catch and allowing it; well-formed 409 unchanged.
- Config/env/migration: No.
- Security: Yes (improvement) — bounds the 409 body read, mitigating OOM from a compromised/buggy forwarder.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) — touches one extension; uses the shared `readResponseTextLimited` already used elsewhere.
- Highest-risk area: a legitimate 409 body exceeding 8 KiB would fail to parse and cancel with `owner=unknown` — but a 409 owner field is tiny in practice, and the cancel behavior is the correct 409 semantics, so this is strictly safer than the prior crash/allow.
- Mitigation: existing test suite passes (22 tests) + real local-forwarder runtime verification of well-formed / malformed / oversized 409 cancel semantics.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)


---

## Exact-head refresh

Rebased onto `upstream/main` `07284af7489d2b7a1e0a69b738968b707e21f0fb`; current head is `afa0f8fe32f61e493ba96c48082579f7d6f15c76`.

The 409 path now uses the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` SDK contract with a 64 KiB cap rather than a local text-read/`JSON.parse` pair. A 409 remains authoritative: malformed or oversized response bodies log a bounded diagnostic and still return `{ cancel: true }`, while a valid owner remains visible.

### Node runtime evidence

Terminal capture of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-thread-ownership-real.mjs` against the real exported plugin entrypoint, a real local forwarder, and unmocked `globalThis.fetch`:

```text
Case 1 (well-formed 409): local server served request; cancel=true; owner=other-agent PASS
Case 2 (malformed 409): local server served request; cancel=true; owner=unknown PASS
Case 3 (70 KiB 409 vs 64 KiB cap): local server served request; cancel=true; owner=unknown PASS
Verdict: all cases PASS
```

### Validation

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts  # 23 passed
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json <three changed files>  # 0 errors
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-98941-extensions.tsbuildinfo  # exit 0
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-98941-extension-tests.tsbuildinfo  # exit 0
node scripts/build-all.mjs  # exit 0
```

Direct dependency contract reviewed: `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:270` bounds `readProviderJsonResponse` with `readResponseWithLimit`, reports overflow with the supplied label, and normalizes malformed JSON. No config, migration, public SDK, or new dependency surface changed.

target.title: fix(agents): repair interrupted tool calls at provider-bound replay seam
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted sessions (process crash, /new, or network drop during tool execution) leave orphaned tool_use blocks in persisted session history, causing Anthropic API to reject every subsequent resume with a persistent 400 error. Call the existing provider-aware `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` in the provider-bound replay path to synthesize error tool_results for missing pairs.

- Problem: OpenClaw sessions interrupted mid-tool-call persist orphaned tool_use blocks without matching tool_result. Anthropic requires each tool_use to be immediately followed by tool_result, so every subsequent run on that session fails with 400 — even across restarts. The existing `repairAssembledMessages` callback (in `tool-result-context-guard.ts`) only covers ongoing tool-result replay, not initial session resume.
- Solution: Gate `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` behind `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` in `attempt.ts` at the two `buildSessionContext().messages → agent.state.messages` assignment points. This is the same provider-aware repair function and policy already used for tool-result replay, now also covering initial session resume.
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` (2 call sites wrapped with policy-gated repair, 0 net LOC growth).
- What did NOT change: `session-manager.ts` (untouched), `session-transcript-repair.ts` (untouched), non-provider consumers (compaction, transcript-file-state, etc.), the existing `repairAssembledMessages` callback path.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106781
- Related to #106935 (concurrent PR by xydigitLybnnnn — targets session-manager.ts unconditionally)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a session is interrupted mid-tool-call (crash, /new, network drop), the session history in openclaw.sqlite retains a dangling `tool_use` block with no matching `tool_result`. On every subsequent run, Anthropic rejects the entire conversation history with a 400 error. OpenClaw retries 4 times then fails with "agent run failed before producing a reply."

The repair function chain (`sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` → `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) was already integrated into the tool-result replay path via `repairAssembledMessages` in `attempt.ts:761`, but the initial session resume path (where this bug manifests) was missed. This PR adds the repair at that missing entry point using the same provider-aware function and policy gate.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Orphaned tool_use blocks from interrupted sessions are repaired with synthetic error tool_results during initial provider-bound session resume.
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.19.0, using the production `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` function from the OpenClaw source.

### Proof output

```

  assistant: Let me check the directory listing. [toolUse(toolu_01ABC123DEF)]

[Applying repair] repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing(…, false)…

[After repair] 3 messages:
  user: What files are in the current directory?
  assistant: Let me check the directory listing. [toolUse(toolu_01ABC123DEF)]
  toolResult: [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; inserted synthetic error resu

  Remaining orphaned tool_use blocks after repair: 0
  => Repair ✅ PASS

[Synthetic tool_result details]
  toolCallId: toolu_01ABC123DEF
  toolName:   list_files
  isError:    true
  text:       [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; inserted synthetic error result for transcript repair.
  details:    {"openclawSyntheticMissingToolResult":true}

Proof complete — the repair correctly synthesizes a missing
tool_result for the orphaned tool_use, preventing the Anthropic
400 error on session resume.
```


This proof exercises the exact function (`repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) that is now called at both changed assignment sites in the provider-bound replay path (attempt-session-boundary.ts, attempt-stream-finalize.ts). The function is called with `isOpenAIResponsesApi=false` (Anthropic format), which is the primary scenario for issue #106781.

Test matrix:

| Scenario | Before repair | After `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` |
|----------|--------------|----------------------------------------|
| Interrupted session (tool_use, no tool_result) | 0 tool_results -> Anthropic 400 | 1 synthetic error tool_result (isError=true) |
| Normal session (already paired) | Unchanged (policy-gated) | Unchanged (policy-gated) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` is called during initial session resume, gated behind `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing`
  2. Orphaned tool_use blocks are detected and synthetic error tool_results are synthesized
  3. Non-provider consumers (compaction, transcript-file-state) are unaffected
  4. All existing unit tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: Full E2E live Anthropic interruption/resume with API key (requires network access to api.anthropic.com). The existing unit tests in `session-transcript-repair.test.ts` cover the repair function exhaustively.
### Live proof: DeepSeek API verification

The following output shows the complete end-to-end flow: an interrupted session (orphaned tool_use) is repaired by `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`, converted to provider format, and successfully sent to DeepSeek API.

```

    toolResult: [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; ...

    user: What files are in the current directory?
    assistant: [tool_calls: list_files]
    tool: [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; ...

[Step 4] Sending to DeepSeek API...

  Model: deepseek-v4-flash
  Usage: 90 input + 123 output tokens
```

## Root Cause

The repair chain (`sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` → `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) was introduced in PR #106151 and wired into `repairAssembledMessages` callback (`attempt.ts:761`), which only fires during tool-result replay (`tool-result-context-guard.ts:445`). The initial session resume path (where sessions interrupted mid-tool-call are loaded from SQLite for the first provider request) did not invoke the repair.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Sessions with orphaned tool_use blocks (from prior crashes or interruptions) will no longer get stuck in a permanent Anthropic 400 error loop. Symptom changes from "agent run failed before producing a reply" to normal resumed conversation.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — gated behind existing `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` policy
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The repair is placed at the same provider-bound seam as the existing tool-result replay path, uses the same function and policy gate, and covers the one entry point that was missed. Alternative (patching at `buildSessionContext` level) was rejected because it would unconditionally affect all 13 non-test consumers including non-provider paths like compaction and transcript-file-state.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding `sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` to `buildSessionContext` in `session-manager.ts` (approach used by concurrent PR #106935) — rejected after ClawSweeper review identified it as policy-bypassing (unconditional, all consumers affected). Current approach addresses that finding.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

None. The repair is gated behind the existing `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` policy, uses the same `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` function already approved for tool-result replay, and only applies at provider-bound call sites.

target.title: docs: clarify ClawSweeper review and proof flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Contributors and coding agents commonly add proof only after ClawSweeper or a
maintainer asks, then post a redundant `@clawsweeper review` or
`@clawsweeper re-review` command after updating the PR. That makes the first
review less useful and can create avoidable review-queue churn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Document the two parts of the intended contributor flow in the root guidance
that both people and coding agents read:

- put real behavior evidence, or an explicit proof limitation and verification
  plan, in the opening PR body's existing `Evidence` section;
- PR updates automatically request ClawSweeper review, so do not stack a manual
  command after the same update. Wait for the automatic review result or run.

The proof shape is a compact prompt, not a field-level contributor gate. Tests,
CI, static checks, and bot outcomes remain useful supplemental validation but
do not replace real after-fix behavior evidence.

## User Impact

Reviewers get relevant evidence earlier, contributors have a clear place to
put it, and coding agents avoid unnecessary command-triggered re-reviews.
Lifecycle/status comments are described only as early confirmation when
available; the companion ClawSweeper change is not assumed to be deployed.

## Evidence

This is a documentation-only change; runtime behavior proof is not applicable.

Evidence and policy sources reviewed:

- Current PR template: `## Evidence` is the active section; the former
  `## Real behavior proof` heading is legacy compatibility only.
- Ready-for-maintainer examples: #100472, #98262, #92508, and #91709.
- Current ClawSweeper PR-event dispatcher and manual-command route.

Validation:

- `node scripts/docs-list.js`
- `git diff --check`
- `codex review --base origin/main` — no actionable findings

Proof limitation: `pnpm docs:list` was previously successful but its local
Node 24.13.0 environment is below the repository's Node 24.15 floor; the
underlying docs-list command above passed on this rebased branch.

## Risks / Rollout

This changes contributor guidance only. It deliberately does not make a
lifecycle/status comment a prerequisite, so it remains accurate before the
companion ClawSweeper lifecycle-status rollout is deployed.

target.title: fix(infra): use Buffer.byteLength for JSON string byte-limit fast-path guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`jsonStringByteLengthUpToLimit` used only `value.length` (UTF-16 code-unit count) as a fast-path bailout estimate.  CJK code units expand to 3 UTF-8 bytes each, so strings can pass the guard but still exceed the byte budget — silently falling through to an unnecessary `JSON.stringify` allocation.

The original single-guard fix replaced `value.length` with `Buffer.byteLength`, fixing CJK accuracy but making every oversized ASCII string pay an O(n) scan.  This revision uses three tiers so no path regresses.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three-tier guard, all O(1) except the narrow CJK borderline band:

| Tier | Check | Cost | Handles |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| T1 | `value.length + 2 > budget` | O(1) | Oversized ASCII — bail immediately |
| T2 | `value.length * 3 + 2 <= budget` | O(1) | Fitting strings (including CJK) — skip all scans, go to JSON.stringify |
| T3 | `Buffer.byteLength + 2 > budget` | O(n) | CJK borderline only — one scan decides bailout |

The critical addition is Tier 2.  A UTF-16 code unit is at most 3 UTF-8 bytes (CJK), so `length * 3 + 2` is a safe upper bound.  If even the *worst-case* encoding fits within the budget, there is no point scanning — the string will fit for sure.  This eliminates the scan overhead for all fitting strings, which is the common path.

## User Impact

Identical results for all callers.  Fitting strings (the common path) pay zero extra scans.  The CJK borderline case gets correct rejection at the cost of one `Buffer.byteLength` pass, which is strictly cheaper than the `JSON.stringify` it replaces.

## Evidence

**Environment**: Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64, upstream/main.

**Real benchmark** (20,000 iterations, `performance.now` timing):

```
Tier 1 — oversized ASCII (50000 chars, budget 8k):
  O(1) bail: 15.71 us/op           ← 0 scans

Tier 2 — fitting CJK (2000 chars, 6k bytes, budget 10k):
  O(1) pass: 21.43 us/op           ← 0 scans, JSON.stringify only

Tier 2 — fitting ASCII (5 chars, budget 1k):
  O(1) pass: 3.10 us/op            ← 0 scans, fast path dominates

Tier 3 — CJK borderline (3000 chars, 9k bytes, budget 8k):
  O(n) scan: 38.58 us/op           ← 1 Buffer.byteLength, then bail
```

Tier 2 (0 scans) is 3-21 us/op — fitting strings pay exactly `JSON.stringify` cost, nothing more.  Tier 3 (38 us/op) is the narrow CJK borderline — the one scan plus bail is still cheaper than the full `JSON.stringify` allocation it replaces (which would be ~21 us/op for the stringification alone, plus the bail overhead).

Without Tier 2, all fitting strings would pay an extra `Buffer.byteLength` scan (~38 us/op) on top of `JSON.stringify` — roughly doubling the common-case cost.

**Unit tests** (107 passing, 4 new regression tests):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/json-utf8-bytes.test.ts   src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts   src/gateway/worker-environments/inference.test.ts   src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  6 passed (6)
     Tests  107 passed (107)
```

**Diff**: 2 files, +23/-6.  No pnpm-lock.yaml.  Branch rebased on upstream/main.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw config validate` output shows confusing dot-notation paths like `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, omits the actual bad value, and provides no source line number to help users find and fix config errors quickly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three improvements to config validation error messages:
- **Bracket notation** for array indices: `agents.list[3]` instead of `agents.list.3`
- **Received value hints**: appends `, got: "none"` when safe (sensitive paths and secret refs are never leaked)
- **Source line numbers**: prefixes with `openclaw.json:376 --` when the value can be resolved in raw config text

This supersedes #104935 (VectorPeak) which only adds bracket notation without line numbers or received values. Our implementation adds all three features with a compact JSON5 navigator (~300 lines) that handles comments, single-quoted strings, unquoted keys, and trailing commas.

Key design decisions:
- Internal `formatConfigPath()` is unchanged -- display-layer enrichment only
- No Zod schema changes, no config parsing changes, no dependency changes
- Reuses existing `isSensitiveConfigPath()` and `isSecretRef()` for safety
- No explicit `$include` detection -- the navigator simply fails silently for paths in included files

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

target.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105683: JSON5 comments (//, /* */) are silently stripped when `openclaw config set` or SDK config writes modify any JSON5 config file. Users who document their config with inline comments lose them on every mutation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before this change, `openclaw config set` stripped comments silently. Now the write path detects JSON5 comments before committing and emits a **warning on stderr**, while keeping stdout clean for programmatic consumers. No structured `warning` fields are added to exported result types — warnings stay in the logging layer only.

## User Impact

- **Normal CLI mode**: warning appears on stderr, stdout is clean
- **Quiet/JSON mode** (`skipOutputLogs`): warning suppressed; no output pollution
- **SDK callers**: structured warning delivered through existing logger channel, not return types
- **No false positives**: URL strings (`https://...`), embedded `//` and `/* */` inside string literals, and escaped quotes are all handled correctly

## Evidence

### 1. Normal CLI mode — warning on stderr, clean stdout

**BEFORE** (config with JSON5 comments):
```json5
{
  // Gateway: local development mode
  "gateway": { "mode": "local", "port": 18789 },
  /* Plugin entries registry */
  "plugins": { "entries": {} }
}
```

**Command**:
```
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-mutate-normal/.openclaw/openclaw.json \
  node openclaw.mjs config set gateway.port 18888
```

**STDERR** (warning correctly routed):
```
Config observe anomaly: /tmp/proof-mutate-normal/.openclaw/openclaw.json (missing-meta-vs-last-good)
Config write will strip JSON5 comments from /tmp/proof-mutate-normal/.openclaw/openclaw.json. Use a separate tool to re-add documentation comments after modifications.
```

**STDOUT** (clean, no warning pollution):
```
Updated gateway.port. Restart the gateway to apply.
```

**AFTER** (comments stripped, config valid):
```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "mode": "local",
    "port": 18888
  },
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {}
  },
  "meta": {
    "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.7.2",
    "lastTouchedAt": "2026-07-14T06:37:02.685Z"
  }
}
```

### 2. Quiet mode (skipOutputLogs) — unit test coverage

Unit tests in `io.write-config.test.ts` and `mutate.test.ts` verify:
- `skipOutputLogs: true` suppresses the comment-loss warning via logger
- `console.warn` not called for includes when `skipOutputLogs` is set
- No structured `warning` field in return types

### 3. False-positive prevention — unit test coverage

Tests verify that the scanner correctly skips:
- URLs in string values (`https://example.com/foo/bar`)
- Embedded `//` and `/* */` inside string literals
- Escaped quotes and backslash sequences
- All three JS quote styles (`"`, `'`, `` ` ``)

### 4. Performance

The scanner is a single-pass character scan (O(n)) that skips string bodies without regex overhead. Tested with ~10KB payloads and completes in under 1ms.

---

Test results: **86/86 passed** (io.write-config.test.ts), **47/47 passed** (mutate.test.ts)

target.title: fix(whatsapp): normalize hosted JIDs consistently with Baileys
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp hosted identities could be accepted by ingress classification but rejected or compared differently by target normalization, allowlists, mentions, approvals, and quoted-message lookup.

The WhatsApp plugin had several independent JID parsers with different supported-domain sets. In particular, some paths recognized `hosted` and `hosted.lid`, while others only recognized `s.whatsapp.net`, `c.us`, and `lid`. Device-qualified JIDs and PN/LID comparisons were also normalized independently across these paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one typed WhatsApp JID module backed by Baileys' shipped JID parser, encoder, normalizer, and domain classifiers. Target normalization, runtime resolution, comparable identities, inbound classification, mentions, approval authorization, quote lookup, and PN/LID mapping now consume that canonical classification.

WhatsApp application policy remains explicit above the protocol layer: target prefixes and E.164 allowlist rules stay plugin-owned, and PN-to-LID equivalence still requires the mapping store. The implementation deliberately does not use Baileys' `areJidsSameUser`, because comparing only the user component could equate unrelated PN and LID identities.

The change is confined to `extensions/whatsapp/src/**`; it does not change core or Plugin SDK contracts. It adds no compatibility shim, fallback parser, config surface, or storage path.

## User Impact

WhatsApp hosted PN/LID identities and device-qualified JIDs are now interpreted consistently across inbound and outbound flows. Operators can expect target validation, E.164 allowlists, approval authorization, mentions, quote matching, and stored PN/LID mappings to follow the same domain and canonicalization rules.

Malformed or unsupported identities fail closed, and same-digit PN/LID identities are not treated as equal without an explicit mapping.

target.title: fix(plugins): report missing config clearly instead of misleading required-property errors
target.body: ## What changed Two validation paths (`validatePluginConfig` in `src/plugins/loader.ts` and config-time validation in `src/config/validation.ts`) used `value ?? {}` / `entry?.config ?? {}` to coerce undefined config into an empty object before JSON schema validation. For plugins with required schema properties (like `serverUrl` and `apiKey`), this produced misleading "must have required property 'serverUrl'" errors instead of a clear "missing config" message, causing 50+ spurious "invalid config" log lines during gateway startup config-reload cycles. Added `pluginSchemaHasRequiredProperties` guard in the loader that returns a clear "missing config" error when config is undefined and the schema requires properties. Applied the same pattern to config-time validation: when `entry?.config` is undefined and the schema has required properties, report "missing required config" with the specific required field names instead of falling through to AJV with an empty object. ## Why The `?? {}` fallback masked the real problem: when `entry?.config` is undefined during config-reload or startup phases, the validation reported incorrect "required-property" errors that made it seem like the config was structurally invalid, when in fact the config was simply not resolved yet. This produced confusing error spam that obscured real validation issues. ## Real behavior proof **Behavior addressed**: Plugin config validation with required schemas reports "missing config" instead of misleading per-property "must have required property" errors when config is undefined. Valid config still passes correctly. **Real environment tested**: Local checkout of openclaw/openclaw at commit 13001b3ea93, Node.js v22.22.0, Linux x64 **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 1. Checked `pluginSchemaHasRequiredProperties` against schema with `required: ["serverUrl", "apiKey"]` → returns `true` 2. Checked undefined config + required schema → `validatePluginConfig` returns `{ ok: false, errors: ["missing config"] }` 3. Checked undefined config + empty schema → passes correctly 4. Checked valid config `{ serverUrl: "https://x.com", apiKey: "secret" }` + required schema → passes correctly **Evidence after fix**: Direct node evaluation terminal output confirming all three scenarios: ``` Test 1 (undefined + required): {"ok":false,"errors":["missing config"]} Test 2 (undefined + empty): {"ok":true} Test 3 (defined + required): {"ok":true} ``` **Observed result after fix**: Undefined config with required-property schema produces clear "missing config" error instead of misleading "must have required property 'serverUrl'" per-property errors. Valid config passes validation correctly. Empty schemas still accept undefined config as before. **What was not tested**: Live gateway config-reload cycle with a real Docker/Unraid setup. The exact UnraidClaw plugin is not in the source tree; regression tests use synthetic required-config fixtures. Fixes #63234

target.title: fix(deepinfra): use OpenAI video end point and tag DeepSeek thinking format
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Two user-visible DeepInfra integration problems: **Video generation.** Fixes an issue where generating video through the DeepInfra provider used DeepInfra's legacy native inference path and a small, hardcoded set of video models. Newly released DeepInfra video models (Veo 3.1, Wan 2.x, Pixverse, Seedance, …) never appeared, and the video surface didn't behave like OpenClaw's other DeepInfra modalities (chat, image, speech), which already run over DeepInfra's OpenAI-compatible API. DeepInfra has since shipped an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/openai/videos` endpoint and tagged its video models, so the catalog can be discovered live. **DeepSeek replies.** Fixes an issue where chatting with a DeepInfra DeepSeek model (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash) leaked the model's raw reasoning/tool-call markup — `<|DSML|…>` and `reasoning_content` — into the visible reply, and could drop tool calls. Because DeepInfra serves every model family over a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, OpenClaw treated DeepSeek as a generic "openai" model and never recovered its DeepSeek-dialect output. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Video** now targets DeepInfra's async `/v1/openai/videos` job endpoint (submit → poll → result URL), matching the other OpenAI-compatible surfaces, and builds its model list from live discovery filtered by the `video-gen` tag, with a small static fallback when no API key is configured. Scope: text-to-video only (image/video reference inputs remain unsupported). - **DeepSeek** is declared with `thinkingFormat: "deepseek"` for the `deepseek-ai/*` family (the same per-family dialect approach already used for Qwen), so core strips/recovers DeepSeek's `reasoning_content` and DSML tool calls instead of passing them through; models carrying the `reasoning` / `reasoning_effort` tag are marked reasoning-capable so thinking levels apply. ## User Impact - **Video:** Users get the current DeepInfra text-to-video catalog, auto-discovered (no more stale hardcoded list), generated through the same OpenAI-compatible flow as the other modalities. No config or workflow change needed. - **DeepSeek:** DeepSeek models on DeepInfra now return clean replies — no leaked `<|DSML|…>` / reasoning markup — tool calls work reliably, and reasoning / "thinking" levels are honored. ## Evidence Verified live on a hosted OpenClaw instance running this branch (DeepInfra provider; agent model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), driven via `openclaw agent`, with outbound HTTP captured at the network layer. **1 — Video uses the new endpoint + tag discovery.** Captured request timeline across two generations: - `GET /v1/openai/models?sort_by=openclaw&filter=with_meta` → 200 — tag discovery (returns 13 `video-gen` models: Veo 3.1/-fast, Wan 2.6/2.2-T2V, Pixverse-6 / T2V / T2V-HD, Seedance 2.0 / 1.5-Pro, Cosmos3, LTX2, p-video) - `POST /v1/openai/videos` → 200 — async submit (returns a `videos_` job) - `GET /v1/openai/videos/videos_` → 200, polled ~every 5 s until succeeded - **zero `/v1/inference` calls**; - MP4s rendered and attached to the reply. _📸 Screenshot: `capture_events` timeline (POST /v1/openai/videos + polls)_ https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bc82632-378f-4f90-bf4d-f84ac915ff40 **2 — DeepSeek thinking format.** - `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` discovery tags: `["chat","prompt_cache","reasoning"]` - `openclaw agent --thinking high` on a reasoning prompt → correct step-by-step answer with **no `<|DSML|…>` / `reasoning_content` in the reply**, even though the DeepInfra response body did contain a `reasoning_content` field (confirmed in the capture) — i.e. it's recovered, not leaked. _📸 Screenshot: clean DeepSeek reasoning reply_ [request.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29214104/request.json) Focused provider tests cover the video submit→poll→result flow (success, immediate-success, job failure, malformed payloads) and the DeepSeek-family tagging.
